newsitem.title: USA: IDEC says drug tests show positive results.
newsitem.headline: IDEC says drug tests show positive results.

text.p: IDEC Pharmaceuticals Corp on Monday said its Phase I/II tests of the drug called Primatized, an anti-CD4 monoclonal antibody, showed positive results in patients with chronic, severe asthma.

IDEC and SmithKline Beecham Pharmaceuticals, a unit of SmithKline Beecham Plc, are co-developing the drug, which is also known as IDEC-CE9.1/SB210396. It is currently in Phase III clinical tests for treating rheumatoid arthritis.
The Phase I/II tests were randomized, double-blinded and placebo-controlled. They assessed three dose levels (0.5, 1.5 and 3.0 mg/kg) of one intravenous infusion in 22 patients.

In a statement, IDEC said the clinical investigators saw a significant dose-dependent improvement in lung function (increased morning and evening peak expiratory flow rate) and symptom scores in the 3.0 mg/kg group.
The patients tolerated treatment with the antibody well, and the investigators reported no serious adverse events. Treatment produced a transient decrease in circulating CD4+ lymphocytes.
